summary: John Marshall worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Dulwich College (~1890–1895), King's College (~1895–1900), and the University of Cambridge (~1895–1900). He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.
John Marston is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and other fields. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (~1989–1997) and held a post at El Colegio de México in 1997.

John Muir was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College (~1826–1828) and the University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853) and founded and held a post at the University of Edinburgh.

John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Lopon Tenzin Namdak, Dudjom Rinpoche, Namkhai Norbu, Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Gompo Tsedan, and Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

John Nemec is an Indologist and philosopher of religion. He studied at the University of Rochester, UC Santa Barbara, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and the University of Pennsylvania. In ~2006, he became Associate Professor at the University of Virginia.
John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College (~1954–1957). He held a post at SOAS University of London from ~1959 to 1999.

John P. Keenan worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, also studying under Noriaki Hakamaya. He was a Research Fellow at Nanzan Institute (1983–1986) and taught at Middlebury College (~1987–2008).
John Peile was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at St. Bees School, Repton School, Christ's College, Cambridge (~1856–1860), and under Theodor Benfey (~1869–1870).

John Perry is a philosopher who studied at Doane University and Cornell University. He held positions at UCLA (~1968–1972), the University of Michigan (~1972–1974), and served as Professor at Stanford University (~1974–2008).
John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as a Professor at the University of Madras from ~1868 to 1879.

John Powers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. His posts include Grinnell College, Australian National University (~1995–2016), Deakin University (2016–2022), and the University of Melbourne (2022).

John R. B. Campbell works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University (~2001–2009) under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, alongside studying under several traditional and language teachers.

John R. McRae studied Buddhism and Sinology, earning a PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein and studying under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Cornell, Indiana University (~1988–2005), Soka University, the University of Tokyo, and Komazawa University.

John R. Shepherd is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Stanford University (~1973–1981) and held a post at the University of Virginia and its College of Arts and Sciences in ~1989.

John Ronald Newman is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and served as Assistant Professor at New College of Florida (~1990–2018).

John Ross Carter studied Buddhist and religious studies at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith. From ~1972 to 2006, he served as a professor at Colgate University's Chapel House.

John S. Strong works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Hartford International University and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. He held a Fulbright fellowship at the University of Ceylon (1987) and taught at Bates College (1987–1988).
John Shore was an Indologist and historian who succeeded William Jones. He served as President of the Asiatic Society from ~1794 to 1798.

John Stratton Hawley works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Amherst College and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1974–1977) and as Professor at Columbia University (~1986).

John Taber is an Indologist and philosopher. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He held posts at Case Western Reserve University (~1984–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).
